record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For an n-vertex graph G and a specified length l, construct an exact counting algorithm running in O*(1.99^n) time that counts the number of cycles of length l in G, where O* suppresses polynomial factors.

evidence.quote: Count the number of cycles of a given length l in G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\ell$ be a positive integer with $3\le \ell\le n$. A cycle of length $\ell$ in $G$ is a sequence of distinct vertices $v_1,v_2,\dots,v_\ell\in V$ (considered up to cyclic rotation and reflection) such that $\{v_i,v_{i+1}\}\in E$ for all $1\le i<\ell$ and $\{v_\ell,v_1\}\in E$.

Design a deterministic exact algorithm that, given $G$ and $\ell$ as input, outputs the exact number of cycles of length $\ell$ in $G$, and whose worst-case running time is $O^{*}(1.99^{n})$, where the $O^{*}$ notation suppresses factors that are polynomial in $n$. Equivalently, exhibit a constant $c<2$ and an algorithm running in time $O^{*}(c^{n})$ that solves this counting problem, or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.category_tag: Exact exponential algorithms for cycle counting
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not reveal a published exact algorithm counting cycles of arbitrary specified length $\ell$ in an $n$-vertex graph in time $O^*(c^n)$ for any constant $c<2$. Existing work (e.g., the general-purpose algorithm of Giscard–Kriege–Wilson, and surveys on faster/space-efficient exact exponential algorithms) addresses related cycle-counting tasks but does not appear to settle the $O^*(1.99^n)$ bound for counting $\ell$-cycles. The status therefore appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: A General Purpose Algorithm for Counting Simple Cycles and Simple Paths of Any Length
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm with running time O(N+M+(ℓ^ω+ℓΔ)|S_ℓ|) for counting simple cycles and paths of any length, parameterized by the number of small connected induced subgraphs rather than by 2^n.
status_evidence.claim: Best known general algorithm is parameterized by structural quantities, not a uniform O*(c^n) with c<2.

status_evidence.title: Faster and Space Efficient Exact Exponential Algorithms: Combinatorial and Algebraic Approaches
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of exact exponential algorithms; counting cycles of specified length is discussed among open problems without a known O*(c^n), c<2, bound.
status_evidence.claim: No O*(c^n), c<2, algorithm for counting ℓ-cycles is reported in the survey.

status_evidence.title: Counting Cycles on Planar Graphs in Subexponential Time
status_evidence.snippet: Subexponential algorithm specifically for planar graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Improvements over 2^n are known only in restricted graph classes, not for general graphs.
